title: How to make an AI see a gibbon
summary: Adversarial examples are inputs with tiny, carefully computed changes that make AI models confidently wrong — like a panda photo classified as a gibbon with 99.3% confidence.

scenes.text: Change an image invisibly — and the AI sees something else.
Image classifiers learn statistical patterns in pixels. They don't see the way we do.
In a famous 2014 example, researchers added carefully computed noise to a photo of a panda.
scenes.reveal: To us: still a panda. To the AI: a 'gibbon', with 99.3% confidence.

items.title: Physical world
items.detail: In tests, stickers on stop signs fooled models

scenes.text: Models can be trained to resist such attacks — but it remains an open problem.
High confidence is not the same as understanding.

sources.title: Robust Physical-World Attacks on Deep Learning Models
